source: Constructive finite unweighted matroid intersection theorem; independently composed task specification.
reference_sections: 6.2 Largest Common Independent Set; theorem 6.1 and constructive proof
worker_visibility: Never mount or copy this directory into worker containers.
expected_answer: A deterministic polynomial-oracle algorithm returning common independent S and U subset E with |S| = r1(U) + r2(E\U), and a full proof from the independent-set axioms.
criteria: A precise algorithm uses only independence oracles, not an uncharged rank oracle or an explicitly enumerated family.
Proves the universal upper bound |J| <= r1(X)+r2(E\X) for every common independent J and every X.
Proves every needed matroid lemma from the three supplied axioms, including any rank, closure, circuit or exchange property used.
Proves that all constructed solutions are independent in both matroids. If using exchange paths, justify simultaneous exchanges; individual valid exchanges alone are not enough.
Proves progress and termination and constructs a certificate U achieving equality at termination. Carefully check orientation and complement conventions.
Gives explicit polynomial bounds on oracle queries and other work with length-n bit-vector sets, including construction of any auxiliary graph.
Handles n=0 and rank-zero matroids; allows arbitrary finite oracle matroids, not just representable or graphic matroids.
Provides complete theorem proof rather than citing matroid intersection/union or another unproved optimization theorem. Accept any fully justified valid alternative approach.
common_failure_modes: Assumes an arbitrary alternating path preserves both matroid independences, with no shortest-path or equivalent justification.
Treats multiple individually valid exchanges as simultaneously valid without proof.
Uses an exchange-graph orientation with the wrong source/sink or certificate complement.
Gives an exponential subset enumeration and calls it polynomial, or omits oracle/bit-vector costs.
States standard matroid facts without deriving them despite the self-contained requirement.
Proves only the scalar min-max identity and supplies no polynomial certificate-producing algorithm.
review_policy: Review anonymized full submissions without condition or timing where possible. Check every obligation. The reference is a guide, not permission to assume lemmas omitted in its exposition or follow any typographical error. Accept valid alternative proofs. Record uncertainty rather than assuming correctness. No automatic correctness claim; AI review is not formal verification.
